title: Texas registration for anyone paid to solicit investors in a Rule 506 offering
rule: Texas's Rule 506 exemption covers securities registration. The State Securities Board says an issuer using it is not a dealer, nor are its owners, directors, officers and employees, but only if not hired to sell, selling only incidentally, and paid entirely for other duties. It says no pay may go to anyone soliciting investors in Texas under Rule 506 unless licensed in Texas as a dealer or agent. Anyone else offering or selling in Texas must register unless exempt, and buyers may sue unregistered sellers to rescind. Finder registration, a restricted dealer registration for individuals, allows pay only for introducing accredited investors, without negotiating, advising, advertising or holding funds.

citation.authority: Tex. Gov't Code 4004.051, 4004.101 and 4008.051; 7 Tex. Admin. Code 109.13(k), 114.4(g), 115.1 and 115.11; State Securities Board, Exemptions from Registration
